title.es: Leer el tiempo en unas memorias

es: Interpretar qué tiempo verbal marca hábito, acción en curso o hecho anterior en un texto breve de memorias, leído y escuchado.

vocabulary.es: se dio cuenta, me di cuenta

teaching.en: In my memoir, I wrote that I used to live in a tiny flat in Lisbon, although in hindsight it was hardly big enough for two people.
teaching.es: En mis memorias escribí que solía vivir en un apartamento diminuto en Lisboa, aunque visto en retrospectiva apenas era lo bastante grande para dos personas.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to + verbo base cuenta un estado o hábito pasado que ya no existe; in hindsight añade la valoración de hoy.
segments: In my memoir, I wrote that I used to live in a tiny flat
in Lisbon, although in hindsight it was hardly big enough for two people.
teaching.audioText: In my memoir, I wrote that I used to live in a tiny flat in Lisbon, although in hindsight it was hardly big enough for two people.

teaching.en: Every morning I would walk to the river, and I remember vividly how the light changed; it became a habit I never questioned.
teaching.es: Cada mañana caminaba hasta el río, y recuerdo con nitidez cómo cambiaba la luz; se convirtió en una costumbre que nunca cuestioné.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo base cuenta una acción repetida en el pasado; vividly describe lo claro que es el recuerdo.
segments: Every morning I would walk to the river, and I remember vividly
how the light changed; it became a habit I never questioned.
teaching.audioText: Every morning I would walk to the river, and I remember vividly how the light changed; it became a habit I never questioned.

teaching.en: I was walking home one evening when I realised that I had left my keys at the bakery, and by then it had started to rain.
teaching.es: Una tarde volvía andando a casa cuando me di cuenta de que había dejado las llaves en la panadería, y para entonces ya había empezado a llover.
teaching.explanationEs: Was walking es la escena en curso; had left es lo anterior; by then sitúa un hecho respecto a otro punto del pasado.
segments: I was walking home one evening when I realised that I had left
my keys at the bakery, and by then it had started to rain.
teaching.audioText: I was walking home one evening when I realised that I had left my keys at the bakery, and by then it had started to rain.

teaching.en: Gradually the streets stopped feeling foreign, although it took me almost a year to settle in properly.
teaching.es: Poco a poco las calles dejaron de parecerme extrañas, aunque me costó casi un año instalarme de verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Gradually marca un cambio lento; settle in es adaptarse a un lugar nuevo hasta sentirlo propio.
segments: Gradually the streets stopped feeling foreign, although it took
me almost a year to settle in properly.
teaching.audioText: Gradually the streets stopped feeling foreign, although it took me almost a year to settle in properly.

teaching.en: Looking back, I feel nostalgic about that year, even though I was working long hours and had already given up on the idea of a proper holiday.
teaching.es: Al mirar atrás, siento nostalgia de aquel año, aunque trabajaba muchas horas y ya había renunciado a la idea de unas vacaciones de verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Was working presenta una etapa en curso; had given up es anterior; nostalgic expresa el sentimiento actual sobre ese pasado.
segments: Looking back, I feel nostalgic about that year, even though I was working long
hours and had already given up on the idea of a proper holiday.
teaching.audioText: Looking back, I feel nostalgic about that year, even though I was working long hours and had already given up on the idea of a proper holiday.

teaching.en: Her grandmother used to tell stories every night, and that habit shaped the way she wrote her memoir decades later.
teaching.es: Su abuela solía contar historias cada noche, y esa costumbre marcó la manera en que escribió sus memorias décadas después.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to + habit: una costumbre pasada; el pasado simple (shaped, wrote) cuenta lo que ocurrió como consecuencia.
segments: Her grandmother used to tell stories every night, and that
habit shaped the way she wrote her memoir decades later.
teaching.audioText: Her grandmother used to tell stories every night, and that habit shaped the way she wrote her memoir decades later.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué hacía el narrador cada mañana?

choices.text: He bought bread and ate it beside the river every day.
He baked bread at home before leaving for his work.
He woke to the smell of bread, then walked by the river.

feedback.es: Every morning + would wake up y used to walk describen costumbres: se despertaba con el olor a pan y paseaba junto al río antes de trabajar.

hint.es: Busca would y used to: marcan lo que hacía de forma repetida.

origin.text: When I first moved to Lisbon, I lived in a tiny flat above a bakery. Every morning I would wake up to the smell of bread, and I used to walk to the river before work. One evening I was walking home when it started to rain. By then I had already forgotten my umbrella, so I waited under a tree and watched the street empty. It took me months to settle in, but I remember that evening vividly, because it was the first time the city felt like mine.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me costó meses instalarme, pero recuerdo esa tarde con nitidez.»

feedback.es: Settle in es la colocación para adaptarse a un lugar nuevo hasta sentirlo propio; el verbo va en base tras to.

hint.es: Es el verbo que forma «adaptarse a un lugar» junto con in.

origin.text: The city felt strange at first. It took me months to ___ in, but I remember that evening vividly.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para entonces ya había perdido las llaves.»

answer.text: By then I had already lost my keys
accepted: By then I had already lost my keys
I had already lost my keys by then

feedback.es: By then sitúa el hecho en un momento del pasado y had + participio marca que ocurrió antes de ese momento.

hint.es: Empieza por la marca temporal y usa had + participio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la narradora con «I had already guessed it was her».

choices.text: The call was so routine that she expected it.
Her grandmother had warned her that she would call that day.
She was angry about being interrupted while cooking.

feedback.es: Los domingos la llamada era una costumbre, por eso ya había adivinado quién era: el past perfect señala que lo supo antes de contestar.

origin.audio: Every Sunday my grandmother would call from the village. She used to ask the same three questions, and I used to give the same three answers. One day I was cooking when the phone rang, and by then I had already guessed it was her, because nobody else called at that hour.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del relato con su perspectiva temporal.

pairs: I used to live in a tiny flat.

pairs.es: Estado pasado que ya no existe

pairs: Every morning I would walk to the river.
I was walking home when it rained.
By then I had already left.

pairs.es: Hecho anterior a otro momento del pasado

feedback.es: Cada forma da una perspectiva distinta: used to, un estado pasado; would, una costumbre; was walking, una escena en curso; had left, algo anterior.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué actitud tiene hoy la autora hacia aquel año?

choices.text: She regrets having worked so many hours back then.
She remembers it warmly despite the long hours.
She wishes she had kept her diary for longer.

feedback.es: Looking back y nostalgic muestran cariño hacia aquel año, aunque trabajaba mucho; no hay arrepentimiento ni queja por el diario.

origin.text: Looking back, I feel nostalgic about that year. I was working long hours, and I had already given up on the idea of a proper holiday, yet every evening I would sit by the window and write a few lines in my diary.

prompt.es: Escucha la memoria y elige qué da a entender la narradora al decir que llamaba a su madre.

choices.text: That her mother did not want her to live in another city.
That she was already starting to enjoy the city.
That she hid how lonely she felt from her mother.

feedback.es: Decir que estaba bien, aunque pasaba las tardes vagando sin rumbo, da a entender que ocultaba su soledad a su madre.

origin.audio: At first, I hated the city. I was living alone, and I had left all my friends behind. Every Sunday I would call my mother and say that I was fine, although the truth was that I spent most evenings walking the streets with no destination. Gradually, without any big moment, the streets became familiar, and one day I realised that a neighbour was waving at me as if I had always lived there.

prompt.es: Con la misma memoria, ¿qué función tiene «I had left all my friends behind»?

choices.text: It gives an earlier event that explains her situation then.
It describes a routine she followed during her first months.
It reports something that happened after she had settled in.

feedback.es: Had left es un hecho anterior que explica por qué vivía sola y sentía rechazo por la ciudad al principio.

origin.audio: At first, I hated the city. I was living alone, and I had left all my friends behind. Every Sunday I would call my mother and say that I was fine, although the truth was that I spent most evenings walking the streets with no destination. Gradually, without any big moment, the streets became familiar, and one day I realised that a neighbour was waving at me as if I had always lived there.

prompt.es: Completa: «Poco a poco, las calles se volvieron familiares.»

feedback.es: Gradually señala un cambio lento y sin momento preciso, como explica la frase anterior sobre la ausencia de un punto de inflexión.

origin.text: There was no single turning point. ___, the streets became familiar, and I could not say exactly when it happened.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Yo solía llevar un diario, pero lo dejé a los veinte años.»

answer.text: I used to keep a diary but I gave it up at twenty

feedback.es: Used to + verbo base cuenta un hábito que terminó; el pasado simple gave up informa de cuándo lo dejó.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué da a entender la autora al decir que ya hacía las maletas?

choices.text: That her partner was reluctant and needed persuading.
That she wanted to leave more than she admitted.
That the flat had become too small for them.

feedback.es: Estaba ya haciendo las maletas antes de que su pareja respondiera: por mucho que lo creyera imposible, deseaba irse más de lo que confesaba.

origin.text: From a memoir: 'We had lived in that flat for years, so leaving seemed impossible. Yet when the offer came, I was already packing before my partner had even said yes.'

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué había ocurrido antes de que ella se enterara.

choices.text: Her neighbour had already left the city.
She had already written to her neighbour.
She had already moved out of the flat.

feedback.es: Had already left the flat es el hecho anterior: se había mudado antes de que llegara la noticia por carta.

origin.audio: By then I had already left the flat, so I did not hear the news until Monday. I was living in another city at the time, and my neighbour used to send me letters, which is how I found out.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando era niña, solía vivir en una casa diminuta junto al mar.»

feedback.es: Used to + verbo base cuenta un estado que ya no existe; la mudanza explica por qué terminó.

origin.text: When I was a child, I ___ to live in a tiny house by the sea, but we moved away when I was ten.
